_comment: North Carolina 2026 QAP, NCHFA as administrative agent for the NC Federal Tax Reform Allocation Committee. Competitive scoring is Section IV, PDF pp.13-28. Page numbers are PDF page indices, which match the printed 'N of 37' numbering. Scope note: Section VI (general and underwriting threshold requirements, pp.29-34) is NOT yet extracted; NC_thresholds.json covers the Section IV thresholds only.

track_totals.note: The QAP states no overall maximum. Its stated section maxima are site evaluation 68, tenant rent levels 2, applicant bonus 2, Olmstead 4 and design 30, which is 106 before deductions. Deductions are large and separate: up to -40 for a Section 1602 exchange project with uncorrected noncompliance, -10 for market-rate units, -10 for excess development costs and -3 on site score.

groups.label: Site amenities, capped at the subsection maximum
groups.source_quote: not to exceed the total for subsection (ii)
groups.note: The nine amenity rows are scored independently by driving distance and their maxima sum to exactly 46, the stated subsection maximum. Tribally-appropriated funds and a bus or transit stop each earn within that same cap rather than on top of it: the QAP says both are 'not to exceed the total for subsection (ii)'. Modelled as a capped sum of 46.

groups.label: Quality of design against adaptive re-use
groups.source_quote: The points in this subsection are mutually exclusive with Section IV(G)(2)(c) below.
groups.note: The QAP marks new construction design quality and adaptive re-use as mutually exclusive, 25 points either way.

criteria.heading: Neighbourhood characteristics
criteria.quote: Good: 10 points if structures within a Half Mile are well maintained

tiers.tier_label: Good: structures within a half mile well maintained, or a Redevelopment Project
Fair: structures not well maintained, visible signs of deterioration
Poor: structures blighted or with physical security modifications

criteria.heading: Amenity: driving distance to a grocery
criteria.quote:
Grocery
12pts.
criteria.note: A small town is a municipality under 10,000 people and gets the longer distance bands. The QAP lists the chains that qualify as a grocery.

criteria.heading: Amenity: driving distance to shopping
criteria.quote:
Shopping
7 pts.

criteria.heading: Amenity: driving distance to a pharmacy
criteria.quote:
Pharmacy
7 pts.
criteria.note: Must sell non-medical general merchandise; hospital, specialty and compounding-only pharmacies do not qualify.

criteria.heading: Amenity: second grocery, shopping or pharmacy
criteria.quote:
Other Primary Amenity
5 pts.

criteria.heading: Amenity: restaurant, bank or petrol station with convenience store
criteria.quote:
Service
3 pts.

criteria.heading: Amenity: healthcare
criteria.quote:
Healthcare
3 pts.
criteria.note: Hospital, urgent care, general or family practice, or general dentist. Specialists and clinics inside pharmacies do not qualify.

criteria.heading: Amenity: public park, library or community centre
criteria.quote:
Public Facility
3 pts.

criteria.heading: Amenity: public school
criteria.quote:
Public School 
3 pts.
criteria.note: Non-alternative elementary, middle or high school; charter and magnet schools qualify.

criteria.heading: Amenity: other retail
criteria.quote:
Other Retail
3 pts.

criteria.heading: Tribally-appropriated funds
criteria.quote: A commitment of at least $250,000 in tribally-appropriated funds
criteria.note: An alternative route to amenity points for sites that would not otherwise score, earned within the 46-point subsection cap rather than on top of it.

criteria.heading: Bus or transit stop within a quarter mile
criteria.quote: A bus/transit stop qualifies for 6 points

tiers.tier_label: In service, fixed location, covered waiting area, six days a week, within 0.25 miles on continuous sidewalks
All of the above except a covered waiting area

criteria.note: Earned within the 46-point subsection cap, not on top of it.

criteria.heading: No incompatible use near the site
criteria.quote: 3 points if there is no Incompatible Use
criteria.note: Three distance bands: half a mile for airports, hazardous materials, polluting industry, junk yards, operating landfills, excessive noise and wastewater plants; 500 feet for adult entertainment and similar; 250 feet for substations, frequently used railway tracks, fast roads and transmission lines.

criteria.heading: No negative site features or construction impediments
criteria.quote: 3 points if there are no negative features, design challenges, physical barriers

criteria.heading: Visible to potential tenants and near a building in use
criteria.quote: 3 points if the project would be visible to potential tenants using normal travel patterns

criteria.heading: Traffic controls allow safe access
criteria.quote: 3 points if traffic controls allow for safe access to the site

criteria.heading: Site deemed unsuitable for housing
criteria.quote: Up to 3 points will be deducted from a site deemed to be unsuitable for housing
criteria.note: Applied even where the site meets every other scoring criterion and has zoning and local support.

criteria.heading: Tenant rent levels and RPP
criteria.quote: An application may earn points under one of the following scenarios

tiers.tier_label: High income county: 25% of low-income units at or below 30% AMI
High income county: 15% of low-income units at or below 30% AMI
Moderate income county: 25% of low-income units at or below 40% AMI
Moderate income county: 15% of low-income units at or below 40% AMI
Low income county: 25% of low-income units at or below 50% AMI
Low income county: 15% of low-income units at or below 50% AMI

criteria.note: One scenario only, chosen by the county's income designation. The 2-point high and moderate county tiers are recorded from pp.18-19; the low-income county wording continues on p.19.

criteria.heading: Development costs above the per-unit limit
criteria.quote: The Agency will assess negative points to applications listing more than the following
criteria.note: -10 above $135,000 per unit under Chart A, or above $150,000 under Chart B, which applies to detached houses and duplexes, severe mobility impairment projects, central business district sites, public housing redevelopment, and steel-and-concrete buildings of four or more storeys.

criteria.heading: Market-rate units included
criteria.quote: Ten (-10) points will be subtracted from any full application that includes market-rate units
criteria.note: Waived where market rents run at least 5% above the 80% AMI maximum and the market study supports them, or where a grant or no-payment financing covers the foregone credit equity.

criteria.heading: Applicant bonus points
criteria.quote: An Applicant is entitled to two bonus points as part of the full application submission
criteria.note: The QAP contradicts itself here and the contradiction is recorded rather than resolved: the heading says MAXIMUM 2 POINTS and the first sentence says an applicant is entitled to two bonus points, but the next sentence says 'No application can receive more than one bonus point.' Read together, an applicant holds two points to spread across at most two applications. Worth a reviewer's eye.

criteria.heading: One-bedroom units as a share of the project
criteria.quote: Projects proposing 1 bedroom units as a percentage of the total project units
criteria.note: Part of the Olmstead Settlement Initiative, which the QAP caps at 4 points across subsections (a) and (b).

criteria.heading: Project in a DHHS priority county
criteria.quote: Projects proposed in the following DHHS priority counties will be awarded 1 point
criteria.note: Nineteen counties are listed; seven of them are marked as dropping off the list after the 2026 cycle.

criteria.heading: Section 1602 exchange project with uncorrected noncompliance
criteria.quote: The Agency may deduct up to forty (-40) points from any application
criteria.note: Applies where the applicant, any owner, principal or affiliate is involved in such a project. The largest single deduction in the plan, and discretionary.

criteria.heading: Site layout
criteria.quote: The Agency will award up to 5 points based on its evaluation of the site layout
criteria.note: Judged on where residential buildings sit in relation to parking, amenities, the community building, postal facilities and trash collection, and on whether the layout keeps traffic speeds low.

criteria.heading: Quality of design and construction, new construction
criteria.quote: The Agency will award up to 25 points for new construction projects based on its evaluation
criteria.note: Judged on roof lines, siding and brick variety, porches and railings, and masonry on exteriors. Mutually exclusive with adaptive re-use.

criteria.heading: Adaptive re-use
criteria.quote: The Agency will award up to 25 points based on the following characteristics
criteria.note: Judged on fit with the surrounding streetscape, aesthetics after adaptation, and special design elements new construction could not reproduce. Mutually exclusive with new construction design quality.

criteria.heading: County with the highest cost-burdened low-income renters per credit unit funded
criteria.quote: First Tiebreaker: The county with the highest cost burden low income renters

criteria.heading: Highest number of total units
criteria.quote: Second Tiebreaker: The project with the highest number of total units

criteria.heading: Lowest average income targeting
criteria.quote: Third Tiebreaker: The project with the lowest average income targeting

criteria.heading: Serves tenants with children
criteria.quote: Tenants with Children: Projects that can
criteria.note: Qualifies where at least 25% of units are three or four bedrooms, and only where the market study shows clear demand.

criteria.heading: Intended for eventual tenant ownership
criteria.quote: Fifth Tiebreaker: Tenant Ownership
criteria.note: Requires a detached single-family site plan and a business plan for conversion at the end of the 30-year compliance period. If a tie survives all five, the project requesting less is preferred (wording continues past p.25).
